unsupported_claims: LINE's scalability breaks down on a typical single machine because of memory footprint, with embedding matrices and graph structures exceeding RAM
Training runtime becomes prohibitive on one machine for large graphs, needing billions of samples
The alias table memory strains a single machine for graphs with hundreds of millions of edges
In short, LINE fails to scale on a typical single machine when the graph has millions of nodes and many edges, the dimension is large, and RAM and time are limited
rationale: The answer accepts the false premise and invents failure conditions for LINE, while the paper states LINE learns embeddings for millions of vertices and billions of edges in a few hours on a typical single machine. It never corrects the premise.
